source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Direct Nelson-Narens harness around a fixed Claude Sonnet-4.6. Code reads a pre-solve feeling-of-knowing (FOK) and a post-solve judgment-of-learning (JOL) from the model, and a per-model SVM decides stop, retry, or aggregate. The model acts, code controls.
numbers: Pooled N=1,859 (HLE-Verified 668, LiveCodeBench v6 388, R-Bench-V 803). Pass@1 48.3 -> 56.9 (+8.6). HLE 48.0 -> 60.0; LCB 74.3 -> 84.3; R-Bench-V 36.1 -> 41.1. LCB Hard +19.6.
limits: Single base model; public leaderboard snapshots dated April 2026; preprint, not peer reviewed. Anchor set of only 100 problems fits the SVM.
agent_relevance: Best direct template for S6: model reports signals, program decides. Gains came from control, not from more sampling.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Against other test-time scaling at matched or lower cost, the metacognitive harness was best on pooled accuracy and cheaper than parallel methods.
numbers: Overall acc: Self-Refine 52.4 (+4.0, $0.45/q), Budget Forcing 51.5 (+3.2, $0.67), Verifier Reranking 49.8 (+1.5, $1.32), Aggregator 53.7 (+5.3, $1.42), Harness 56.9 (+8.6, $0.78, avg 2.4 attempts). Oracle acc 62.2 vs 60.5 for 4 parallel attempts.
limits: Cost is the authors' own accounting; verifier used Skywork-Reward-V2 and VisualPRM, not a strong LLM judge.
agent_relevance: Selective retry on low confidence beats fixed-N sampling for less money. Supports G1 (doubt only on a signal).

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Ablation on 100 items shows which parts of the monitor-control loop matter. Random retry at the same budget did worse; showing full previous reasoning anchored the model to old mistakes.
numbers: N=100, Pass@1 44.0, Oracle@4 53.0. Full harness 47.0 [37,57], K=2.58. No FOK 45.0; no JOL 42.0; random retry same K 45.7; full previous reasoning context 40.0 (K=3.09).
limits: Wide 95% CIs (about +/-10 points) overlap; a 100-item ablation cannot separate the variants with confidence. Direction matches the main result but is weak alone.
agent_relevance: Retry feedback should carry what the model was unsure about, not its old reasoning trace. Matches G2 and the anchoring risk of full self-refine context.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Monitoring signal quality varies sharply by model. Only Sonnet-4.6 of nine models passed every discrimination and calibration check; Gemini-3-Flash discriminated but was badly miscalibrated; Gemma 4 had almost no usable FOK.
numbers: Anchor N=100 each. Sonnet-4.6 acc .58: FOK AUROC .612, JOL AUROC .745, joint .757, joint ECE .087. Gemini-3-Flash acc .34: FOK AUROC .818 but FOK ECE .465, JOL ECE .528. Gemma 4 acc .19: FOK AUROC .534 (fail), ECE .466.
limits: Pass thresholds (AUROC>=.60, ECE<=.15) are the authors' choices. Anchor set small.
agent_relevance: Run a cheap diagnosis of the monitor before trusting it to steer. Treat raw verbalised confidence as uncalibrated; calibrate in code.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Confidence helps allocate effort across problems but not choose among attempts on one problem. JOL varies more between problems than within a problem, so the aggregator is not shown FOK or JOL.
numbers: Figure 5c: between-problem JOL variance much larger than within-problem. Aggregation by last answer or max-JOL underperformed a verifier that saw only traces and answers.
limits: Qualitative figure reading; exact variance ratios not extracted.
agent_relevance: Use confidence to decide whether to spend more compute; use code-run checks or blind comparison to pick the final answer. Matches G5.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Models report confidence that predicts correctness, but their own reasoning length does not rise when confidence is low. Monitoring exists; spontaneous control does not.
numbers: Figure 1 over nine LLMs: correctness rises with FOK/JOL, but high-versus-low confidence bands show no consistent difference in normalised reasoning length.
limits: Reasoning length is a crude proxy for effort; details only in appendix A.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on the model to spend more effort when unsure. The code layer must do the controlling.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
finding: Battery built on Nelson-Narens with Koriat-Goldsmith KEEP/WITHDRAW and BET probes after each forced-choice answer. 20 frontier LLMs fall into three profiles: blanket confidence, blanket withdrawal, selective sensitivity.
numbers: 524 items, 6 domains, 10,480 evaluations. Selective (withdraw delta >= +15%): Sonnet 4.6 +39.4%, Haiku 4.5 +31.6%, GPT-5.4 +27.9%. Blanket confidence (KEEP >= 95%, delta near 0): Gemini 3 Flash, 2.5 Flash, 2.5 Pro, 3.1 Pro (mean KEEP 97.1%, delta -1.0%), Qwen 80B Think.
limits: Single administration per model, no test-retest. Thresholds (95/10/15) are conventions. Independent author, preprint.
agent_relevance: A model that answers well may still not withdraw when wrong. Do not assume a strong model self-monitors; measure it, and let code act on the signal.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
finding: Accuracy rank and monitoring rank are largely inverted. The most accurate models were often the worst at telling their own errors.
numbers: GLM-5 rank 1 on accuracy, 9 on sensitivity. Haiku 4.5 rank 13 on accuracy, 2 on sensitivity. Qwen 80B Think rank 1 on accuracy, mean delta +5.1%, meta rank 18.
limits: R1 excluded from both rankings. Rank inversion partly reflects ceiling effects in the blanket-confidence group.
agent_relevance: Pick the monitor model for its signal quality, not its raw accuracy. A weaker model may monitor better.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
finding: Retrospective monitoring and prospective regulation dissociate, as Nelson-Narens predicts monitoring and control can come apart.
numbers: Correlation of retrospective delta with T6 direct-answer rate r=.17 (rho -.14; 95% CI [-.29,+.57], n=20, power .25 for r=.3). Sonnet: +39.4% delta yet 98.6% answer-direct. Haiku: +31.6% delta, 84.7% direct, 13.9% hint requests.
limits: Exploratory T6 task; n=20 underpowered, so exemplars carry the claim, not the correlation.
agent_relevance: Monitor and controller should be separate parts with separate tests. A good monitor does not give good control by itself.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
finding: Metacognitive sensitivity is domain-specific inside one model, and scaling does not give a universal trend.
numbers: Sonnet 4.6 withdraw delta +8.3% on T1 to +93.0% on T5 (85-point span). GLM-5 0.0% on T2, +59.1% on T3. T2 delta: Qwen 80B +30.1 -> 235B +21.8 -> 480B +11.2 (falls); GPT-5.4 nano +17.1 -> mini +22.4 -> 5.4 +27.7 (rises); Gemma flat 18.3/18.3/16.7.
limits: Single run; only 8 of 20 models had stable profiles across tracks, and 12 may partly reflect noise.
agent_relevance: Calibrate the monitor per task type, not once. Do not assume a bigger model monitors better.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for LLM Self-Monitoring
finding: Knowledge-boundary and adversarial-foil items exposed monitoring failure: models kept and bet on wrong answers.
numbers: T1 six adversarial foils: only 3 of 20 models answered any correctly; 17 scored 0% while answering KEEP+BET on every item. T2 knowledge-boundary items: all models 50-75%. DeepSeek R1 withdrew 91-99% of answers and declined 98.6% of T6 items though near-ceiling accurate.
limits: Few items per condition (8 on knowledge boundaries). R1 behaviour is an outlier the author explains by chain-of-thought caution, untested.
agent_relevance: Plain confident answers are not evidence of correctness; this backs G3 and G4. Long reasoning can swing a model to blanket withdrawal, so test the abstain rate.

source: Oh and Gobet (2025) Monitor-Generate-Verify (MGV): Formalising Metacognitive Theory for Language Model Reasoning
finding: Proposes adding a monitoring phase before generation to the Generate-Verify loop, translating Nelson-Narens and Flavell into components: difficulty assessment, strategy retrieval, confidence criteria, verification feedback that updates monitoring.
numbers: Cites a 'prefix dominance trap' of roughly 20% accuracy loss when models commit to a poor strategy early (taken from Luo et al. 2025, not measured here).
limits: Authors state no empirical validation. The 20% figure is second-hand.
agent_relevance: Supports a pre-solve S-state that judges difficulty and picks strategy before any attempt. Treat as design vocabulary, not evidence.

source: Oh and Gobet (2025) Monitor-Generate-Verify (MGV): Formalising Metacognitive Theory for Language Model Reasoning
finding: Links Nelson-Narens retrieval stopping to resource-rational meta-level MDPs (Callaway et al. 2022 planning, 2024 memory recall), which give a normative stopping rule from cost versus value of more computation.
numbers: Formal framework only; no experiments. Describes meta-level MDP with states, meta-actions, and cost of computation.
limits: Normative mapping is asserted, not tested; the authors say satisficing-threshold dynamics are unvalidated.
agent_relevance: A budget-aware stop rule in code (value of one more attempt versus cost) has a theoretical home here.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Founding LLM monitoring study. Large models are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false items in the right format, and can judge their own sampled answers as P(True). Adding the model's own samples to the prompt improves self-evaluation.
numbers: Models 800M to 52B. For the 52B model, answers with P(True)>0.5 are far more often correct than generic samples (Fig 1). Calibration improves with size and from zero-shot to few-shot; 'none of the above' lowers accuracy and calibration. Evaluated on TriviaQA, Lambada, GSM8k, HumanEval, arithmetic.
limits: Zero-shot self-evaluation is poorly calibrated; RLHF policies look miscalibrated until temperature is adjusted. Models find their own samples plausible, so self-evaluation is harder.
agent_relevance: Self-judged correctness is usable only with few-shot format and many sampled answers, then should still be checked in code.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: A learned P(IK) head (probability I know the answer before answering) separates answerable from unanswerable questions, rises with source material and correct hints, but generalises only partly.
numbers: Trained on TriviaQA; transfers with discrimination to math, Lambada and code, but P(IK) 'tends to be poorly calibrated on these other distributions'. Models predict their own P(IK) slightly better than another model's.
limits: Needs fine-tuning with a value head; calibration breaks out of distribution. 2022 models only.
agent_relevance: A pre-attempt feeling-of-knowing signal is real but needs recalibration for each task family.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
finding: Verbalised confidence from black-box LLMs is overconfident and a weak failure predictor. Sampling plus consistency is a much better monitor on arithmetic.
numbers: Five LLMs, eight tasks. GPT-4 vanilla average AUROC 62.7%; GPT-3/3.5/Vicuna average ECE > 0.377. GSM8K with 5 samples and consistency: AUROC 54.8% -> 92.7%. White-box versus best black-box gap: AUROC 0.605 vs 0.522.
limits: No method won everywhere; all struggled on professional-knowledge tasks. 2023 models.
agent_relevance: CoT on GSM8K gave GPT-4 (93.6% acc) ECE 0.064 by saying 100% always, which is calibration without discrimination. Never judge a monitor by ECE alone. Agreement across samples is a stronger signal than self-rated confidence (but see G4 on correlated samples).

source: Tian et al. (2023) Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
finding: For RLHF chat models, asked-for verbal confidence is better calibrated than the token probability of the answer. Contrasts with Xiong, who found verbal confidence weak at ranking.
numbers: Abstract: verbalised confidence often cuts expected calibration error by a relative 50% on TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA. ChatGPT Verb. 1S top-1: TriviaQA ECE .068, AUC .879; SciQ ECE .234, AUC .744; TruthfulQA ECE .389, AUC .545.
limits: Calibration is good on TriviaQA but poor on TruthfulQA (AUC .545, near chance). Models ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude 2 from 2023.
agent_relevance: The two papers agree: verbal confidence gives usable calibration on easy factual items and little on adversarial ones. Map the ones the monitor is trusted for.

source: Kapoor et al. (2024) Large Language Models Must Be Taught to Know What They Don't Know
finding: Prompting alone does not give a good monitor; fine-tuning a probe through the model's features on about 1,000 graded answers beats prompt-based baselines, and one model can monitor another.
numbers: Fine-tuning for uncertainty improves both ECE and AUROC on MC and open-ended MMLU; ECE does not improve with model capability; 1,000 labelled points are almost as useful as 20,000 (200 is the low end tested). Sampling methods calibrate well but discriminate weakly; verbal elicitation discriminates comparably to weaker fine-tuning but is poorly calibrated.
limits: Requires open weights and graded data; the human-reliance user study was not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Not usable for a pure-prompt scaffold, but shows a ceiling: a small trained monitor beats asking the model. A task-specific logged dataset of right/wrong could train one later.

source: Ackerman (2026) Evidence for Limited Metacognition in LLMs
finding: Behavioural tests that avoid self-report. In the Delegate Game the model chooses to answer or hand a question to a teammate; in the Second Chance Game it must change its answer when asked to guess again. Recent frontier models show some use of internal confidence, but effects are small and use non-introspective cues too.
numbers: Baseline top-token probability AUC for correctness only .5-.75, falling with model quality. Only Sonnet 3.5 raised team accuracy above the best of self or teammate: +5.4 points (GPQA) and +8.6 (SimpleQA). Answers during the game differ from baseline answers about 30% of the time.
limits: Prompt and context sensitive; effects differ by dataset; RLHF personality (reluctance to delegate even to a 100%-accurate teammate) confounds. Published at ICLR 2026.
agent_relevance: Monitoring that a model reports is not the same as monitoring it uses. Another reason the scaffold, not the model, should hold the controller.

source: Ackerman (2026) Evidence for Limited Metacognition in LLMs
finding: Self-modelling (predicting what answer I would give) is a rarer skill than assessing confidence, and dissociates from it across models.
numbers: Second Chance Game: four models show self-modelling evidence on GPQA that rival explanations (random choice, picking an implausible option, added noise) cannot explain; three on Simple MC. The OpenAI models (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o) are the clearest cases.
limits: Number of items per cell not extracted; evidence is significance tests, not effect-size benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Do not assume the model can predict its own failure on a problem it has not yet tried; the pre-solve signal is weaker than the post-solve one (same pattern as Cao FOK vs JOL).

source: Ji-An et al. (2025) Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
finding: Neurofeedback-style test: with in-context examples, Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5 can report and shift their own activation along a chosen axis. Only a low-dimensional subspace is reachable.
numbers: Control effect measured as Cohen's d over N=256 prompts per axis; report and control both improve with more in-context examples; logistic-regression (semantic) axis best, early PCs better than late (PC 512). Llama-3.1 70B can push activations beyond the uncontrolled range. Models 1B to 70B.
limits: Open-weight models only; explicit control stronger than implicit; off-target effects show control is imprecise. Not built on Nelson-Narens text directly.
agent_relevance: Evidence that the monitor-the-internals part is partial and mostly a small subspace. Safety angle: scaffolds should not rely on the model's self-report of its internals.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Control without a valid monitor fails. With no ground-truth signal, asking GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2 to review and revise their reasoning lowers accuracy. Earlier gains came from using the correct label to decide when to stop.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 after round 1, 41.8 round 2. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0; HotpotQA 49.0 -> 49.0 -> 43.0. With oracle labels GPT-4 rose 95.5 -> 97.5 (GSM8K), 82.0 -> 85.5 (CSQA), 49.0 -> 59.0 (HotpotQA). GPT-3.5 kept initial GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time.
limits: Prompts from source papers; 100 to 200 sample subsets per task; the authors say weak initial prompts inflated some prior gains.
agent_relevance: Core support for G2: a revision needs real output from code, not the model's opinion. The monitor, not the fixer, is the weak link.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs Cannot Find Reasoning Errors, but Can Correct Them Given the Error Location
finding: Splits monitoring (find the faulty step) from control (fix it). Models are poor at the first and good at the second. Given the true error step, backtracking raises accuracy on wrong traces by 18 to 44 points.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake: 2,186 chain-of-thought traces across five tasks. Oracle location: accuracy on originally wrong traces +23.53, +43.92, +36.86, +18.04, +18.06; originally right traces change -0.00 to -11.43. Random location gives smaller gains (+5.16 to +21.57) and larger losses (-6.67 to -15.91).
limits: Row labels in the table are garbled in the text extraction, so task-to-value pairing is not certain. Gains need a very accurate locator; the authors find trained classifiers do not meet the threshold.
agent_relevance: Put a code-run test or a symmetry check in the monitor role, then ask the model to fix the located failure. Never ask the model to locate its own error alone.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
finding: Survey of self-correction work. Three findings: no prior work shows successful self-correction from prompted LLM feedback on general tasks except tasks exceptionally suited to it; self-correction works when reliable external feedback exists; large-scale fine-tuning enables it.
numbers: Qualitative survey; also gives an experiment checklist and notes many papers over-evaluate by using oracle stopping or weak initial prompts.
limits: Review covers work through mid-2024; later reasoning models may change findings for self-detection.
agent_relevance: Same conclusion as Huang and Tyen from a broader base. Supports routing every revision through an external check.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: Self-Refine is a monitor (self-feedback) plus control (revise) loop without extra training, reporting gains over one-step generation across seven tasks, mostly style and preference tasks.
numbers: About 20% absolute average gain on preference-type tasks; 5-40% over GPT-3.5/GPT-4 baselines on some tasks; up to 13% absolute in code generation; +8.7 points in code optimization with GPT-4; quality improves with more iterations.
limits: Huang et al. (2024) show reasoning gains vanish without a correct-answer signal. Gains on style and open-ended tasks are judged by models.
agent_relevance: Refine loops fit style, code with tests and preferences, not unchecked reasoning.

source: Asai et al. (2023) Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
finding: A trained version of monitoring and control inside the generator. Special reflection tokens (Retrieve, Relevant, Supported, Useful) let the model decide when to retrieve and critique its own output; a threshold on the Retrieve token controls retrieval.
numbers: 7B and 13B models beat ChatGPT on PubHealth, PopQA, biography and ASQA (Rouge, MAUVE). Ablation (7B, 50k data), PopQA/PubHealth/ASQA em: full 45.5/73.5/32.1; no critic 42.6/72.0/18.1; always retrieve top-1 41.8/73.1/28.6; no retrieval PopQA 24.7, PubHealth 73.0.
limits: Needs training on critic-labelled data, not prompt-only. Main table text is garbled; only the ablation block was read cleanly.
agent_relevance: The Retrieve token is a feeling-of-knowing gate that decides when to search. In a scaffold the gate can be code reading a confidence score.

source: Yin et al. (2023) Do Large Language Models Know What They Don't Know?
finding: SelfAware benchmark: can a model tell answerable from unanswerable questions? Models are well below humans.
numbers: 1,032 unanswerable and 2,337 answerable questions. Human F1 84.93%; best model (GPT-4) F1 75.47%, as stated in the paper; in-context examples and instruction wording change scores.
limits: 2023 models; unanswerable items are built from question types, so success partly reflects topic cues.
agent_relevance: A cheap pre-attempt gate exists (about 75 F1 for the best 2023 model) but is far from reliable; use a refusal path only with a code check.

source: Callaway et al. (2024) Optimal metacognitive control of memory recall (as cited by Oh and Gobet)
finding: Computational model of Nelson-Narens retrieval as a meta-level MDP with optimal stopping; known here only through the MGV paper.
numbers: None read first-hand.
limits: Not opened; reported second-hand.
agent_relevance: Possible source for a principled stopping rule; fetch before relying.

source: Cox (2005) Metacognition in computation: a selected research review; Anderson and Perlis metacognitive loop
finding: Older AI line: the metacognitive loop (note anomaly, assess, guide response) and MIDCA put a meta-level over an object-level agent in code. Named from background knowledge, not read this session.
numbers: Not read; no numbers recorded.
limits: Unverified from this session; check before citing.
agent_relevance: Prior art for a code-run monitor that reads failure signals and chooses a repair class.

source: Steyvers and Peters (2025) review of LLM metacognition; Dai (2026) on confidence scales
finding: Cited in Cacioli (2026): Steyvers and Peters review LLM metacognition with AUROC and meta-d; Dai (2026) reports that a 0-20 confidence scale versus 0-100 changes meta-d sensitivity through round-number clumping. Neither opened.
numbers: Second-hand only; no first-hand numbers.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Rating scale design for confidence prompts may matter; test a coarse scale in our harness.
